email.test.subject: Mail Concierge test e-mail
email.test.body:
Hello,

This is a test e-mail sent by Mail Concierge. If you are reading it, e-mail sending works.

cfg.templatesLang: Templates shown: {0}. Templates of other languages are kept as they are.
cfg.native: Do not use Mail Concierge for “Forgot password”
cfg.nativeHint: Jellyfin then keeps its own behaviour: it writes a PIN to a file on the server, and only for requests from the local network. No e-mail is sent.
cfg.publicUrlHint: Every link in e-mails is built from it (for example https://jellyfin.example.org). Nothing is sent while it is empty.
cfg.defaultLanguageHint: Used for e-mails sent to users who have not chosen a language.
cfg.allowAdminsHint: Off by default: administrators can neither reset their password by e-mail nor sign in with their e-mail address.
cfg.sessions: Sessions closed after a password reset
cfg.sessInactive: Only sessions inactive for some days
cfg.secretHint: Write-only. Leave empty to keep the stored value.
cfg.testHint: Save the settings first: the test uses the saved settings.
cfg.err.test_send_failed: the e-mail could not be sent. Check the SMTP host, port, security and credentials; the technical detail is in the Jellyfin log.
cfg.err.test_not_configured: save the public URL, the SMTP host and the sender address first.
cfg.warnSmtpNone: Security “None”: e-mails and the SMTP password travel unencrypted. Use it only on a trusted local network.
cfg.warnHttpPublicUrl: This URL starts with http://: the links in e-mails (recovery, invitations) will travel unencrypted. Use https:// unless this is a private network.
cfg.warnHttpSeerr: This URL starts with http://: the Seerr API key will travel unencrypted. Use https:// unless Seerr is on a trusted local network.

cfg.maxAccount: Recovery e-mails per account per hour
cfg.maxIp: Forgot-password requests per address per 15 minutes
cfg.maxPin: Wrong PIN attempts before the PIN is cancelled

cfg.help.publicUrl: The web address of your Jellyfin server as your family sees it (for example https://jellyfin.example.org), used to build the links in e-mails.
cfg.help.defaultLanguage: The language of e-mails sent to users who have not chosen a language.
cfg.help.allowAdministrators: When ticked, administrator accounts can also reset their password by e-mail and sign in with their e-mail address; leave it off to keep administrators out of both.
cfg.help.sessionsOnReset: Chooses which devices are signed out when someone resets their password: all of them, only the ones inactive for the threshold below, or none.
cfg.help.sessionDays: Number of days without activity after which a device counts as inactive; only used when the option above is the inactivity one.
cfg.help.smtpSecurity: How the connection to the mail server is protected; use the option your mail provider gives you (usually STARTTLS on port 587 or SSL/TLS on port 465).
cfg.help.fromAddress: The e-mail address shown as the sender of the messages Mail Concierge sends; it must be allowed by your mail server.
cfg.help.invitationDays: How long an invitation link stays valid, in days, before it expires.
cfg.help.pinMinutes: How long a recovery PIN code stays valid, in minutes, before a new one is needed.
cfg.help.confirmationHours: How long the link to confirm a new e-mail address stays valid, in hours.
cfg.help.cancelHours: How long the link that lets someone cancel an e-mail address change stays valid, in hours (24 by default). Cancelling also needs the account password.
cfg.help.maxRecoveryHour: The maximum number of password recovery e-mails (code and link, and the notice after a reset) Mail Concierge sends per hour for the whole server. Anyone can request them, so this budget can be used up by abuse, but it never affects invitations.
cfg.help.maxInvitationHour: The maximum number of invitation e-mails Mail Concierge sends per hour for the whole server. Only administrators send invitations, and this budget is separate from the recovery one, so anonymous requests cannot use it up.
cfg.help.maxAccountHour: The maximum number of e-mail address confirmation messages Mail Concierge sends per hour for the whole server. They are triggered by signed-in users. The security notices sent to a replaced address are never counted here.
cfg.help.maxAccount: The maximum number of recovery e-mails one account can receive per hour.
cfg.help.maxIp: The maximum number of forgot-password requests from one internet address in 15 minutes.
cfg.help.maxPin: The number of wrong PIN attempts allowed (a count, not a time) before that PIN is cancelled and a new one must be requested.
cfg.help.templates: The wording of the e-mails Mail Concierge sends: change a template to personalise it, or leave it empty to keep the built-in text.
cfg.help.seerrUrl: The web address of your Seerr server (for example http://seerr:5055), used to match Jellyfin accounts with Seerr users.
cfg.help.seerrApiKey: The secret key found in Seerr under Settings, General, which lets Mail Concierge talk to Seerr; it is stored securely and never shown again.
cfg.help.assignProvider: Makes Mail Concierge the password-reset method of every eligible account in one click, so the e-mail reset works for everybody.
cfg.emailLogin: Allow sign-in with the e-mail address
cfg.emailLoginShared: {0} confirmed address(es) are shared by several accounts and cannot be used to sign in.
cfg.emailLoginUnavailable: Not available with this Jellyfin version: the sign-in action was not recognised. Signing in with the user name is not affected.
cfg.help.emailLogin: If ticked, a user can type their confirmed e-mail address instead of their user name on the sign-in screen of any app. An address shared by several accounts cannot be used. After 3 failed sign-ins on the account (fewer if its lockout threshold is low), the address stops working until the user signs in with their user name. Mail Concierge does not limit or ban sign-in attempts: put fail2ban or an equivalent in front of Jellyfin.
